compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

configs.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships it, cover fitted.
configs.name: base

configs.description: 13930-701 - Velocity single-sided horizontal cable manager, 1U, black.
configs.name: black

gaps.note: the data sheet says two cable openings are in the rear; no held page gives their size or position, so the two obrounds are estimates (80 wide, the usable height high, at a quarter and three quarters).
no held page counts or dimensions the fingers: 5 a row at a 90.0 pitch is read by eye from a small grey render and is one more or less.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned plan view, or a larger photograph

gaps.note: the notes give a usable depth of 94 mm and a usable height 31 mm under the overall height; they do not say where the depth starts or that the 31 is split equally between the two finger plates.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned section of the manager

gaps.note: the table's note says the overall height is ".03 inches (0.16 mm)" under the full rack unit; the two figures differ (0.03 in is 0.76 mm). The full unit is drawn.
gaps.wanted: the maker's drawing, to say which figure is meant

gaps.note: the cover snaps on and "stays in the opened position" when swung out; the format has no hinge, so it is drawn as one fitted plate that lifts off, and the swing is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover, and a close picture of the cover's edge

gaps.note: the data sheet lists four #12-24 and four M6 rack-mount screws and gives no hole positions.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the back plate

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.

gaps.wanted: no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - the material (plastic) and finish ("black plastic") are the data sheet's specifications table and "Color is Black" its note; the indoor-only statement is its description row.

bottom.note: estimated - the same fingers along the bottom as along the top; the bottom is the top again.

chassis.note: datasheet - 1U x 19 in x 5.9 in (150 mm) for 13930-701 in the ordering table. The width is the 482.6 of 19 in EIA, ears included, as a rack-face part is its ears and what hangs off them. The height is the 44.45 of 1 unit at 1.75 in. The table's note says the overall height is less than the full unit by ".03 inches (0.16 mm)", two figures that disagree (0.03 in is 0.76 mm); the full unit is stated and the difference, under a millimetre, is a gap. The depth is the table's overall figure.

color.note: estimated - "Color is Black" (the table's note); the shade is the near-black the other Velocity parts use. The data sheet's photograph of the part is a grey render.

door.note: datasheet - "One cover that snaps onto the T-shaped cable guides" and "the snap-on cover stays in the opened position to provide easy access to cables" (data sheet, pages 1 and 2). The cover is its own part, fitted as shipped, so a drawing can take it off and show the fingers; the format has no hinge, so how it swings is a gap.

ears.note: estimated - the 16.3 of ear each end is half of the 32.6 between the 450.0 the manager's body is taken to fill (the EIA-310 clear opening between the rails, 17.72 in) and the 482.6 overall. No document gives the ear width. Their mounting holes are not drawn.

fingers.note: estimated - T-SHAPED FINGERS, TOP AND BOTTOM, ON THE FRONT ONLY. The data sheet says the manager has "T-shaped cable guides (fingers)" and its photograph shows them along the upper and lower edges. No page counts them: 5 a row at a 90.0 pitch (four slots) is read by eye and is one more or less. The finger plates are 15.5 thick, half of the 31 mm by which the usable height is less than the overall height. The slot and head are estimates.

front.note: estimated - the cover, fitted. With it off, the two rows of finger heads. The `duct` guide is the 13.45 between the finger plates over the 450.0 between the ears.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on the front view is the channel between the finger plates, run across the rack; finger pitch 90.0 and slot 36.0 as `fingers`.

left.note: estimated - the side: the back plate, the two finger plates 15.5 high with the usable height between them, and the cover's face and returns at the front. No page gives a side elevation.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET TABLE AND NOTES; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM ITS PHOTOGRAPH. The Velocity Cable Management product data sheet (page 3, Single-Sided Horizontal Cable Managers table) prints 13930-701 as 1U x 19 x 5.9 in (150 mm), shipping weight 2 lb (0.9 kg), with notes on colour, height, usable depth and usable height; page 1 lists what the manager includes and page 2 describes it. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: the fingers, the cover, the ears and the rear openings are estimated, each in its own entry below, and the photograph is a grey render. Nothing was copied from a picture; the figures are transcribed.

mount.note: datasheet - the data sheet lists "Four #12-24 x 1" rack-mount screws and four M6 x 25 mm rack-mount screws" and "One 19"W EIA rack-mount cable manager", so the part bolts to the rail face at a rack unit and stands out from it, which is what `rack-face` says. No held page gives the hole positions.

passes.note: estimated - the two openings are open (`cover: open`): a cable crosses the back plate through each from the front to the rear. The sizes are those of `rear` above.

rear.note: estimated - the data sheet says "Two cable openings in the rear of the manager allow front-to-rear cabling" and no held page gives their size or position. They are drawn and declared as two obround openings 80 wide and 13.45 high (the usable height), a quarter and three quarters of the way across the body. Every figure of them is an estimate; see the `rear-openings` gap.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides.

shell.note: estimated - A SHEET BODY, NOT A BOX: the back plate as a well 148.0 deep, the two rows of fingers standing in it, and the cover across the finger heads, which snaps off.

thickness.note: estimated - no document states a gauge; 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in this library.

top.note: estimated - the plan, rear at y=0: the back plate 2.0 thick, the finger plate to 144.0, four slots 36.0 wide on a 90.0 pitch from 56.0 to 138.0 deep with rounded roots, narrowing to the 12.0 neck under the cover. The depths are the table's and notes'; the slots are read off the photograph.

usable.note: estimated - the table's notes give a usable depth of 3.7 in (94 mm) and a usable height 1.2 in (31 mm) less than the overall height at the narrowest point. The slots end 56.0 out (150 less 94) and the finger plates are 15.5 each; the notes do not say where the 94 starts or that the 31 is split equally.

weight.note: datasheet - 2 lb (0.9 kg) in the ordering table, whose column is SHIPPING weight: the carton is in it, so the manager itself weighs less. It is stated as the weight so the part has one, and is an upper bound.
